entities.summary:
Sri Mara, also known as Khu Liên or Ou Lian, was a foundational figure in the early history of the kingdom of Lâm Ấp, which was established in 192 AD.

A local official of Xianglin under the Chinese Eastern Han dynasty, Sri Mara rose to prominence as a key leader in the region's political landscape, utilizing his administrative expertise to shape the kingdom's early development.

The kingdom of Lâm Ấp would go on to play a significant role in the broader Southeast Asian region, with Sri Mara's legacy influencing the cultural, economic, and political trajectory of the area for centuries to come.

One of the most striking aspects of Sri Mara's significance is his ability to navigate the complex web of regional politics, forging alliances with neighboring kingdoms and balancing the competing interests of powerful dynasties.

Despite the passage of time, Sri Mara's impact on the region remains evident, with his name still invoked in contemporary discussions of Southeast Asian history and politics.
